newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee strengthens on dollar and pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee strengthens on dollar and pound.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee firmed against both the dollar and the pound on Friday, reflecting support of the local currency by central bank market intervention, forex dealers said.
The rupee was posted at a mean commercial rate of 20.2765 against the dollar from 20.3145 on Thursday. The rupee firmed to a mean of 33.4040 versus the pound from 33.5035 on Thursday.

Forex dealers said the rise of the rupee against the dollar was the result of regular market intervention by the central bank during the past few weeks. The central bank sold dollars to commercial banks on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday this week. Last week, the central bank also intervened on three occasions.
"The rupee is rising against most major currencies like the dollar, pound, (French) franc, deutschemark...interventions are supporting the value of the rupee," one dealer said.

The dealer said the stronger rupee against the dollar also reflected the weaker U.S currency in international markets. "You can say the rupee is appreciating because of a combination of both international trends and market interventions."
With the regular market intervention, commercial banks were seen as being square in the foreign exchange reserves and were able to meet demand from their customers (importers).
